the detector is segmented in six identical cells to measure the energy spectrum at different distances from the compact core

physics_goals.quote: aiming at testing the hypothesis of light sterile neutrinos as an explanation of the deficit of the observed neutrino interaction rate with respect to the predicted rate
physics_goals.value: Test whether a light sterile neutrino explains the Reactor Antineutrino Anomaly by comparing antineutrino spectra of six cells at 9-11 m from a compact 235U-enriched reactor core

summary.plain: A detector divided into six cells, ten metres from the compact core of the research reactor at the Institut Laue-Langevin in Grenoble, built to test whether the missing reactor antineutrinos turned into a hypothetical sterile neutrino. It ran from 2016 to 2020 and rejected that explanation.
summary.technical: Very-short-baseline (9-11 m) reactor antineutrino experiment: six optically separated Gd-loaded liquid-scintillator cells at the 58.3 MWth, highly 235U-enriched ILL research reactor, comparing cell-to-cell spectra largely independently of flux predictions. Data 2016-2020; rejects the Reactor Antineutrino Anomaly best fit (>99.9 % CL) and measures the 235U spectrum.
